basis: Strip 1, line 1 (large type): the samekh's inside is empty, so there is no dagesh. B's סֶּ adds a dot that isn't printed. The samekh carries a segol, and there seems to be a small vertical stroke next to it, which matches A's meteg.

Strips 1 and 2, line 'קמה תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד': the resh has a hataf-patah under it (a short bar with two dots), not a plain shva. This printing visibly uses hataf-patah for shva in these בר/הל forms. B's וַאֲבָרְכָה turns it into a familiar spelling that isn't printed.

Strip 2, line 2: the resh in אברכך has a hataf-patah, and so does the first lamed in ואהללה. Both are clearly not plain shva. There seems to be a meteg beside the segol under the kaf, which matches A. B's plain shvas and missing meteg don't match the print.
Strips 4 and 5, line 'יי כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וַחֲסִידֶיךָ': the resh has a hataf-patah. B's יְבָרְכוּכָה doesn't match the print. A's meteg on כֽוּ fits the small mark under that letter.
Strip 9, last line 'עוֹלָם הַלֲלוּיָהּ:': the first lamed has a hataf-patah, not a shva. Both readings have the mappiq in the final he, so that isn't in dispute.
